pr_title: Bluetooth: audio: ascs: Fix missing ASCS/ASE cleanup
pr_body:
This adds fixes for ASE/ASCS cleanup that was missing in few places.
The unit tests have been added that trigger invalid behavior fixed in this PR.

Fixes: #56111
Fixes: #56138
Fixes: #56139
Fixes: #51552

issue_context.title: LE Audio: unicast_server listen incorrect behavior
comments: @MariuszSkamra Are you intending on fixing this?

review_comments: Can we be sure that `ase->ep.iso` is not NULL here?

I see that there was no check for ISO not being NULL before my change.
Looking int the code, the ISO gets assigned in `ase_stream_qos` function context. Thus I would say the pointer is valid.
But I consider adding assert here.
Can we be sure that `ase->ep.iso` is not NULL here?

I see that there was no check for ISO not being NULL before my change.
Looking int the code, the ISO gets assigned in `ase_stream_qos` function context. Thus I would say the pointer is valid.
But I consider adding assert here.
Could consider implement a `stream_conn_get_role(stream)` too
I assume that the _SAFE version is chosen here in case that the callback removes an ASE?

As it's used inside of `bt_ascs_foreach_ep`, one cannot say that it won't be used to remove the entries from the list - eg. upper layer will call `bt_bap_unicast_server_release` from `bt_bap_ep_func_t` context. Thus it's better to use _SAFE version of the iterator.
Why is this better than having a separate function for it?

I explained in the commit message:
```
This removes redundant bt_ascs_ase_get_from_slab function and moves it's
functionality to ase_new(). It's sane, because the ASE shall be
allocated from ase_new() function context only.
bt_ascs_ase_return_to_slab() has been renamed to ase_free() to follow
the naming convention. Furthermore, few logs have been fixed/added.

```

Am I missing something here? 
The _SAFE macros make sense to use when removing something from the list, but from what I can tell, the ASES are not being removed from `session` here, so can't we just just the non-SAFE version?
`ase_release(ase);` call removes it from the list.

Ah, yes, because `ase_release -> ascs_ep_set_state(BT_BAP_EP_STATE_RELEASING) -> ascs_ep_set_state(ep, BT_BAP_EP_STATE_IDLE) -> ase_free` 

Given the fairly long list of function calls here (including a recursive one) where the change to `BT_BAP_EP_STATE_IDLE` is conditional, I think we should add a comment here :)
Can we be sure that `ase->ep.iso` is not NULL here?

I see that there was no check for ISO not being NULL before my change.
Looking int the code, the ISO gets assigned in `ase_stream_qos` function context. Thus I would say the pointer is valid.
But I consider adding assert here.

Why are we storing this here now, rather than using the one from `bap_unicast_server`? I know they point to the same structure, but the callback has intentionally not been put into ASCS. Ideally ASCS should work independently of the BAP Unicast Server (not possible right now), but this approach creates a stronger coupling.

Fair - Agree to disagree :D 

In any case, there is a strong coupling right now, and since this doesn't really change that, it's fine :)
